# Best chargers for charging lots of AA/AAA NiMH cells at once

**My pick for most people: a 16-bay charger with independent slots.** Two 8-bay units also work. The sources are affiliate review sites, not hands-on lab tests, so treat the rankings as a shortlist.

## 16 bays (most batteries at once)
- **BONAI 16-Bay.** It takes AA and AAA mixed in any slot, with any number of cells. Output is 250-500 mA per port, input is 110-240V AC, and each port has an LED for charging, full, or a faulty cell. It won't charge alkaline or lithium cells. ([source](https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-nimh-aa-battery-charger/))
- **Tenergy TN438 16-Bay.** It has an LCD showing each cell's status, protection against overcharge, overheating, short circuits, and reverse polarity, and an 8-hour timer. It's a good choice if you want to see what each cell is doing. ([source](https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-nimh-battery-charger/))
- **POWEROWL 16-Bay.** It has 16 independent channels and a four-stage charge (pre-charge, quick, floating, trickle). ([source](https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-aa-battery-chargers/))
- **CITYORK 16-Bay.** It has a smart LCD and a heat-dissipating design. ([source](https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-nimh-battery-charger/))

## 8 bays (cheaper and smaller)
- **Tenergy TN480U 8-Bay.** It has an LCD, 500 mA per AA and 250 mA per AAA, and USB-C or Micro-USB input. It costs $23.99 at Tenergy's official store, and the price was checked on 2026-10-21. **[Buy the Tenergy TN480U](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-tn480u-8-bay-nimh-charger)** (an affiliate link, at no extra cost to you). It has a 12-month warranty and 30-day returns, but you pay return shipping. ([source](https://dealectric.com/tenergy-tn480u-8-bay-nimh-charger))
  - It doesn't include a power adapter. You need a 5V/2A USB charger, or five or more AA cells will drop to 250 mA each on a 1A source.
- **EBL 8-Bay.** It has per-slot LEDs (red charging, green full, flashing red bad cell) and MCU-controlled safety cutoffs. ([source](https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-aa-aaa-charger/))

## Things to know
- Look for independent slots, so one weak cell doesn't hold up the rest.
- Only NiMH and NiCd cells work in these chargers, never alkaline or lithium.
- I don't have direct purchase links for the 16-bay models. The source pages list "Check Price on Amazon" buttons, but the product URLs weren't in my search results. You can find them through the linked articles, or by searching the model names above.
- For the 16-bay chargers, I'd lean toward the **Tenergy TN438** for the per-cell LCD, or the **BONAI** if you want the simplest AC-powered setup. Check current prices and recent reviews before buying.

If you tell me how many cells you typically charge and whether you use high-capacity ones like Eneloop Pro, I can narrow it down.
